subject.title: feat: Force reply to originating channel (Telegram/Discord/WhatsApp)

question: Should OpenClaw make external-origin reply delivery a durable automatic invariant, add an explicit opt-in force-origin/fallback policy, or keep the current WebChat and same-surface gates with narrower channel-specific fixes?
rationale: The next change decides when generated content may leave an internal/dashboard surface for an external conversation selected from stored route state, so code inspection cannot safely choose the privacy and product boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Adopt durable turn-origin delivery
options.body: Capture the inbound turn's external route once, preserve it through execution, and deliver final replies there unless the turn explicitly chooses another route, with route freshness and authorization safeguards.

options.title: Add opt-in force/fallback policy
options.body: Keep current defaults but add documented default-off force-origin or fallback delivery with schema, doctor/docs, route freshness, authorization, and live-channel proof.

options.title: Keep current gates
options.body: Leave WebChat and same-surface suppression as the default boundary and address only proven channel-specific delivery defects such as WhatsApp same-surface drops.

recommendation.title: Adopt durable turn-origin delivery
recommendation.body: Capture the inbound turn's external route once, preserve it through execution, and deliver final replies there unless the turn explicitly chooses another route, with route freshness and authorization safeguards.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already made the prior product call on the persisted-origin PR and is the clearest routing decision owner from the available history and discussion.
